'''Carlton Kaleel''' "'''Bub'''" '''Carrington III''' (born July 21, 2005) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh Panthers]] and was selected by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the first round of the [[2024 NBA draft]] before being traded to the Wizards during the draft.

==Early life==
Carrington was born on July 21, 2005, in [[Baltimore, Maryland]].<ref name="auto4">{{Cite web |title=Carlton Carrington |url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/carlton-carrington/12728 |access-date=November 30, 2024 |publisher=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Carlton Carrington |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4845374 |access-date=November 30, 2024 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> The third in his family with the same name was nicknamed "lil' bub" after his basketball coach father's nickname, later shortened to just "bub."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Carter |first=Christopher |date=October 12, 2023 |title=Guards Jaland Lowe and Carlton Carrington learn from physical practices and past Pitt leaders |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2023/10/12/panthers-basketball-jaland-lowe-carlton-carrington-ncaa-college-hoops-acc/stories/202310110094 |access-date=November 30, 2024 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite news |last=Hiles |first=Noah |date=November 23, 2023 |title=Pitt freshmen thankful to play in front of family during Thanksgiving trip to Brooklyn |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/Pitt/2023/11/23/bub-carrington-jaland-lowe-thankful-thanksgiving-brooklyn-nit-season-tipoff/stories/202311230076 |access-date=November 30, 2024 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref> He attended [[Saint Frances Academy (Baltimore)|Saint Frances Academy]] in Baltimore, where he played basketball, baseball and football.<ref name="auto4"/> He was also part of the chess club. He scored over 2,000 points in his high school career, and after his [[Junior (education year)|junior]] year, committed to playing college basketball for [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], being ranked by [[247Sports]] as a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], the 99th-best recruit overall, and the third-best player from the state.<ref name="auto4"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Cobb |first=David |date=June 15, 2022 |title=Pitt basketball recruiting: Four-star CG Carlton Carrington commits to Panthers in 2023 class |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/pitt-basketball-recruiting-four-star-cg-carlton-carrington-commits-to-panthers-in-2023-class/ |access-date=November 30, 2024 |work=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref><ref name="auto1">{{Cite magazine |last=Thompson |first=Stephen |date=June 15, 2023 |title=Four-Star G Carlton Carrington Commits To Pitt |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/recruiting/pitt-basketball-carlton-carrington-commits-panthers |access-date=November 30, 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=McGonigal |first=Johnny |date=June 16, 2022 |title=Panthers sign Carrington for 2023 |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-post-gazette/135718680/ |access-date=November 30, 2024 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |page=C9 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> He chose Pittsburgh over eight other offers.<ref name="auto1"/>

Carrington was also a member of Team Melo in the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] travel circuit, being named the EYBL Breakout Player of the Session and second-team All-Session while helping the team reach a spot in the championships.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Thompson |first=Stephen |date=July 15, 2022 |title=Pitt Basketball Commit Carlton Carrington Named EYBL Breakout Player of Session |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/recruiting/pitt-basketball-commit-carlton-carrington-named-eybl-breakout-player |access-date=2024-06-28 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> As a [[Senior (education)|senior]] at Saint Frances in 2022–23, Carrington helped the school have an overall record of 29–11 while going 11–3 in the [[Baltimore Catholic League]] (BCL); he was named first-team All-BCL and to the BCL All-Tournament team and averaged more than 26 points, seven rebounds, six assists and two steals per game.<ref name="auto4"/> He also led Saint Frances to the [[Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (MIAA) tournament, which they won for the second time in his tenure, with Carrington being named to the All-Tournament team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 25, 2023 |title=Carrington Named to Capital All-Star Team |url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2023/3/25/mens-basketball-carrington-named-to-capital-all-star-team.aspx |access-date=November 30, 2024 |publisher=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]}}</ref> He had shooting splits of .490/.380/.860 and set a Saint Frances record with more than 1,000 points scored.<ref name="auto4"/> He was invited to the DTLR Classic, Jumpman Classic, R1A Classic, more than Basketball Game and to the MLK Classic, earning [[most valuable player]] honors in each while setting an MLK Classic record with 42 points scored.<ref name="auto4"/><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Hines |first=Jam |date=January 17, 2023 |title=High School Spotlight: 2023 Saint James MLK Classic Eye-Catchers (Part One) |url=https://www.si.com/nba/draft/newsfeed/high-school-spotlight-2023-saint-james-mlk-classic-eye-catchers-part-one |access-date=November 30, 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He was named a Capital All-Star, played at the 50th Annual Hoop Culture Capital Classic, and was All-Tournament at the City of Palms and Triple Threat Classics.<ref name="auto4"/>

==College career==
Carrington joined the Pittsburgh Panthers for the start of the [[2023–24 Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball team|2023–24 season]] and became an immediate starter.<ref name="auto2">{{Cite magazine |last=Thompson |first=Stephen |date=November 6, 2023 |title=Bub Carrington Makes Pitt History in College Debut |url=https://www.si.com/college/pittsburgh/basketball/bub-carrington-makes-pitt-panthers-history-college-debut |access-date=November 30, 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> He started in the exhibition opener against the [[University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown]] and the regular-season opener against [[North Carolina A&T Aggies men's basketball|North Carolina A&T]]. Against North Carolina A&T, he helped the Panthers win 100–52 while totaling 18 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists for the first [[triple-double]] in a debut in school history and the second in [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) history, also being the first overall to accomplish the feat at Pittsburgh since 1998.<ref name="auto2"/><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 6, 2023 |title=Carlton Carrington triple-double paces Pitt in opener |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/basketball/carlton-carrington-triple-double-paces-pitt-opener-2023-11-07/ |access-date=November 30, 2024 |work=[[Reuters]] |via=Field Level Media}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Carter |first=Christopher |date=November 7, 2023 |title=Freshman Bub Carrington is the first player in Pitt hoops history to record triple-double in debut |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/2023/11/07/panthers-college-hoops-mens-basketball-acc-bub-carrington-jeff-capel/stories/202311060101 |access-date=November 30, 2024 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 13, 2023 |title=Carrington Named ACC Rookie of the Week |url=https://pittsburghpanthers.com/news/2023/11/13/mens-basketball-carrington-named-acc-rookie-of-the-week.aspx |access-date=2025-01-01 |publisher=[[Pittsburgh Panthers]]}}</ref> He was named the ACC Rookie of the Week and received the honor again the following week, being the first Pittsburgh player to earn selection back-to-back since 2007–08.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{Cite news |date=November 21, 2023 |title=ACC keeps noticing Pitt freshman |url=https://www.altoonamirror.com/sports/local-sports/2023/11/acc-keeps-noticing-pitt-freshman/ |access-date=November 30, 2024 |newspaper=[[Altoona Mirror]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 26, 2024, Carrington was selected with the fourteenth overall pick by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]. He was later traded, along with [[Malcolm Brogdon]], to the [[Washington Wizards]] for [[Deni Avdija]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Cohn|title=Baltimore's Carlton 'Bub' Carrington selected No. 14 overall by Washington Wizards in 2024 NBA draft|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2024/06/26/carlton-bub-carrington-nba-draft/|work=The Baltimore Sun|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=June 26, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Wizards Complete Trade with Trail Blazers|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-complete-trade-with-trail-blazers|website=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2024|access-date=July 6, 2024}}</ref> On July 7, he signed with the Wizards.<ref>{{cite web|first=Alex|last=Kirschenbaum|title=Wizards' Carlton Carrington Signs Rookie Contract|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/wizards-carlton-carrington-signs-rookie-contract.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=July 7, 2024|access-date=July 16, 2024}}</ref> 

In his rookie season Carrington was one of only 11 NBA players who played in all 82 games.<ref>{{cite web | last=O'Donnell | first=Ricky | title=11 NBA iron men who played all 82 games this season, including an old and tiny Chris Paul | website=SB Nation | date=2025-04-14 | url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2025/4/14/24408190/nba-players-all-82-games-appear-ironman-chris-paul-mikal-bridges | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2024-25 Player Stats |url=https://www.nba.com/stats/players/traditional?SeasonType=Regular+Season|access-date=2025-05-22 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> He finished the year posting averages of 9.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and 4.4 assists per game. In May 2025 he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].<ref>{{cite web |date=May 20, 2025 |title=Stephon Castle, Zaccharie Risacher headline NBA All-Rookie First Team |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2024-25-all-rookie-teams-announced |access-date=20 May 2025 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

In his second season Carrington likewise played in all 82 games, becoming the first player since [[Karl-Anthony Towns]] in 2016-17 to appear in every game in each of his first two seasons.<ref>{{cite web |date=April 12, 2026 |title=Tomlin scores career-high 26 as Cavaliers defeat Wizards 130-117 in regular-season finale|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/2026/04/12/wizards-cavaliers-score/466c826c-36d0-11f1-90c4-9772c7fabc03_story.html|access-date=April 14, 2026 |first=Joe|last=Reedy|website=washingtonpost.com}}</ref> He finished the year averaging 10.7 points, 3.4 rebounds, and 4.6 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Carrington is the son of Carlton 'Bub' Carrington (died 2025) and Karima Carrington.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vukovcan |first1=Mike |date=March 21, 2025 |title=Pitt Basketball Basketball Community Mourning Death of ‘Big Bub’ Carrington II, Father of Pitt Star |url=https://pittsburghsportsnow.com/2025/03/21/pitt-basketball-community-mourning-death-of-big-bub-carrington/ |access-date=March 22, 2025 |website=Pittsburgh Sports Now}}</ref> He has two siblings, Kareem and Faith.<ref name="auto4"/> Carrington is a second cousin of retired NBA player [[Rudy Gay]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gorman |first=Kevin |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Behind leading scorer Blake Hinson, Pitt hoops enters season with a standard of expectations |url=https://triblive.com/sports/behind-leading-scorer-blake-hinson-pitt-hoops-enters-season-with-a-standard-of-expectations/ |access-date=November 30, 2024 |newspaper=[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]}}</ref>
